note: Forward-looking ledger of Liberal April 2026 financial-crime announcements (federal financial-crime police agency, federal crypto-ATM ban) reframed against the eight-year arc of named gaps (2018 OAG money-laundering finding through 2024 TD Bank guilty plea and 2024-2026 FINTRAC budget cut). Schema is locked: each row tracks announcement -> mandate -> first-named-target -> first-named-prosecution-or-closure. Empty cells are honest cells. Page evolves as chronology resolves.

rows.announcement: OAG Spring 2018 Report 1 — money-laundering enforcement-gap finding
rows.promised_by: Office of the Auditor General of Canada (Spring 2018, Report 1); Government response acknowledged enforcement gap.
rows.mandate_published: yes — OAG report itself is the published mandate
rows.first_named_prosecution_or_closure: still announcing in 2026 — see 2026-04-28 and 2026-04-30 rows

rows.promised_by: Hon. Austin F. Cullen, Commissioner of Inquiry, 2022-06; 101 recommendations accepted in full by BC government — acceptance is not implementation.
rows.mandate_published: yes — final report + 101 recommendations published; per-recommendation implementation status (in-force / partial / not-yet) is the open follow-up
rows.first_named_target: institutional — BCLC, GPEB, named ministers Coleman/Bond/de Jong
rows.first_named_prosecution_or_closure: no criminal conspiracy charged; 2026 federal announcements do not name BC casinos or Vancouver real-estate channel; BC-side status of the 101 recommendations a separate open question

rows.announcement: OAG report on FINTRAC (referenced as 2023 / Spring 2024 "Combatting Money Laundering")
rows.promised_by: Office of the Auditor General; FATF mutual-evaluation echo. Found FINTRAC had not shared enough intelligence with police; real-estate sector lacked tools; reporting entities non-compliant.
rows.mandate_published: yes — OAG report enumerated specific gaps
rows.first_named_target: no named target — finding addressed FINTRAC capability gaps and bank/real-estate/casino non-compliance generically
rows.first_named_prosecution_or_closure: still announcing in 2026 — 2026-04-30 federal financial-crime agency re-promises what FINTRAC was supposed to already do
rows.deep_link_status: pending — OAG search-page URL patterns 404 from external probes

rows.announcement: TD Bank guilty plea (US DOJ) — money laundering
rows.promised_by: U.S. Department of Justice (October 2024); TD Bank pleaded guilty — largest Canadian bank in history to plead to money laundering. Paid $3B+ in fines.
rows.mandate_published: yes — US DOJ filed and concluded
rows.first_named_prosecution_or_closure: delivered IN U.S., not Canada. Canadian regulators (OSFI/FINTRAC) did not detect what US DOJ prosecuted; this is the "delivered elsewhere" datapoint that frames the 2026 federal-agency announcement.
rows.deep_link_status: pending — DOJ press-release URL probes return 403/404 from external fetchers

rows.promised_by: Carney Government, 2024-2026; budget reductions while FINTRAC's mandate (offshore money-laundering tracking) remained on the books. Concurrent with Brookfield-routed pension flows.
rows.mandate_published: opaque — defunding executed without a public mandate change
rows.first_named_target: no target — this is a removal-of-capacity row, not a new-mandate row
rows.first_named_prosecution_or_closure: 2026 announcement re-promises capacity that was concurrently being cut — most damning datapoint between the 2023 OAG finding and the 2026 announcement

summary.thesis_one_line: Eight years of named gaps; zero federal Canadian criminal prosecutions of named officials; the only delivered enforcement was in U.S. courts; capacity was concurrently being cut while new agencies were being announced.
